question: Is pembrolizumab in any Phase 3 lung cancer trials, and what are its common adverse reactions?

route.reason: The question asks whether pembrolizumab appears in Phase 3 lung cancer trials (trial registry information) and also asks for its common adverse reactions (drug label information), so both sources are needed.

draft.text: Yes. ClinicalTrials.gov lists 144 Phase 3 studies matching pembrolizumab and lung cancer [count:1]. Examples: NCT03302234, pembrolizumab with ipilimumab or placebo in untreated metastatic NSCLC (KEYNOTE-598), Phase 3, completed [trial:NCT03302234]; NCT06561386, nivolumab and relatlimab plus chemotherapy vs pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy in stage IV/recurrent non-squamous NSCLC, Phase 3, recruiting [trial:NCT06561386]; NCT01905657, two doses of pembrolizumab vs docetaxel in previously treated NSCLC (KEYNOTE-010), Phase 2/3, completed [trial:NCT01905657]. The label excerpts provided do not give a clean list of the most common adverse reactions overall. In the KEYNOTE-671 lung cancer neoadjuvant/adjuvant setting, the label reports fatal adverse reactions in 1.3% of patients [label:pembrolizumab:adverse_reactions:30]. Adverse reactions leading to permanent discontinuation included acute kidney injury, interstitial lung disease, anemia, neutropenia, and pneumonia [label:pembrolizumab:adverse_reactions:30]. In the adjuvant phase, the most frequent serious adverse reaction was pneumonia (3.4%), and discontinuations were due to diarrhea, interstitial lung disease, AST increased, and musculoskeletal pain [label:pembrolizumab:adverse_reactions:31]. The excerpts do not include the full common adverse reaction table for lung cancer.
